source.title: SWAD: Domain Generalization by Seeking Flat Minima
source.authors: Junbum Cha; Sanghyuk Chun; Kyungjae Lee; Han-Cheol Cho; Seunghyun Park; Yunsung Lee; Sungrae Park

record.tranche_reason: Tests flatness-aware training in domain generalization and reports results on unseen domains, a setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies domain shift, which the claim excludes as out-of-distribution generalization. Its local-flatness measure and unseen-domain results do not test the listed versions' same-distribution train-test gap or V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Figure 3 values are only plotted; the text describes their ranking.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima premise to develop SWAD, but does not test any listed version. Its local-flatness statistic measures expected loss changes under spherical perturbations, rather than V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and ranking of train–test gaps. Domain-shift accuracy and the additional in-domain accuracy results do not supply that test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that seeking flat minima improves domain generalization and report that SWAD finds flatter solutions and improves benchmark performance. They also derive robust-risk bounds and report in-domain improvements, while acknowledging that SWAD is a heuristic without a guarantee of finding flat minima.
record.recipe_differences: Uses dense, overfit-aware stochastic weight averaging for domain generalization; evaluates local flatness and unseen-domain performance rather than the original claim's same-distribution gap or specified interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences across datasets and training-domain/target-domain splits; SWAD's averaging start and end depend on validation-loss monitoring. Its ablation finds performance changes when dense sampling and start/end scheduling are removed.

fits_no_version.finding: On PACS, the authors report lower average local-flatness values for SAM and SWA than ERM, with SWAD lowest across the experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SWAD reduces expected loss sensitivity to the paper's spherical weight perturbations relative to the compared methods on PACS.

fits_no_version.finding: PACS out-of-domain accuracy rises from 85.3% for ERM to 85.9% for SWA and 87.1% for SWAD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight averaging improves held-out-domain accuracy under the tested PACS protocol.

fits_no_version.finding: SWAD improves ImageNet-C mCE from 57.6 to 55.7, BGC accuracy from 8.7% to 11.8%, and ImageNet-R accuracy from 36.7% to 38.8% relative to ERM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SWAD improves robustness on the tested ImageNet corruption, background, and rendition benchmarks.

record.problems: The paper describes SWAD as a heuristic approximation without theoretical guarantees as a flatness-aware solver. Figure 3 values are plotted without tabled numeric values; the flatness estimate uses 100 Monte-Carlo samples. Experiments are in domain-generalization or robustness settings, not the listed same-distribution claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were selected from the extensive benchmark tables because those results concern domain-shift comparisons and do not test any listed version. Figure 3 is represented with figure-only rows; plotted numerical values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and natural-label generalization under matched recipes.
Width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout additions or removal and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket description of the experiments as exclusively domain-shift or robustness evaluations is incorrect: Tables 3 and 5 include in-domain test accuracy, and Table 6 includes clean ImageNet accuracy. These still do not test a listed version. No additional version-relevant results require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Large-batch generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and same-distribution train-test gap.

relation.reason: SWAD operationalizes a related flatness premise, but the study's results do not measure any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study uses the flat-minima premise to develop SWAD and evaluates local loss sensitivity and domain-generalization performance. Neither its spherical perturbation statistic nor its robust-risk bounds test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of train–test gaps; no other listed version is tested.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate, including SWAD's heuristic limitation. Figure 3 supports qualitative flatness rankings, not numerical point estimates or V7; R11–R15 are method-performance comparisons outside the listed versions.
